briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax-Relief Momentum Builds in Lansing While Rescheduling Survives Its First Court Test
briefs.top: In Michigan, GOP nominee John James is courting cannabis donors with a pledge to gut the 24% wholesale tax just as new data shows the levy badly missing revenue targets — giving repeal advocates fresh ammunition heading into November. Nationally, a federal appeals court just upheld marijuana's Schedule III reclassification, Curaleaf's takeover bid for Aurora is reshaping the MSO landscape, and psychedelic medicine keeps racking up regulatory wins.

local.text: Republican gubernatorial nominee John James is promising to repeal or sharply cut Michigan's 24% wholesale cannabis tax, a pledge that's already got industry donors opening their wallets for his campaign even without a replacement plan for road funding.

Product innovation is paying off for operators: Michigan cannabis beverage sales hit $2.1 million in July, up 27.2% year-over-year — the fastest-growing category in the state — led by brands like Mary Jones, Keef Cola and CQ.

Hospitality-driven retail is still expanding despite the tax squeeze — Fields Cannary's Muskegon dispensary-restaurant buildout is moving forward toward a fall opening, a bet that experience-led cannabis retail can outrun the margin crunch.

Jars Cannabis, a 54-store chain spanning Michigan, Arizona and Colorado, reached an agreement with Madison Heights to remove a surveillance camera required under a prior licensing settlement — a small but real compliance win for operators negotiating with skeptical municipalities.

The wholesale tax is badly missing its own projections — about $37 million in Q2 and $34 million in Q1 against an initial $105 million-per-quarter estimate — handing the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's ongoing Court of Appeals challenge and the broader repeal push real momentum.

national.text: A legal challenge to marijuana's Schedule III reclassification was rebuffed this week: on Sept. 9 the D.C. Circuit left the medical marijuana rescheduling order fully in effect, rejecting arguments from anti-rescheduling forces.

Consolidation is accelerating: Curaleaf's takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis, launched Aug. 10 and formally commenced Aug. 18, would create a combined platform with pro forma revenue exceeding $1.5 billion — a clear signal MSOs are thinking bigger and more global.

The FDA is holding a public hearing Sept. 14 on the future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs, the latest step in a regulatory push that's already put psilocybin and methylone on an accelerated approval track.

Compass Pathways just named the recipients of its U.S. grant program to train healthcare providers on delivering COMP360 psilocybin therapy, building the workforce infrastructure needed ahead of a potential first-ever FDA approval of a classic psychedelic.

Operators dodged a bullet on hemp: the federal ban on hemp THC products, originally set for Nov. 12, has been pushed back to Dec. 11 under a bill President Trump signed last week, buying the industry more runway.
